statements.subject: participant
statements.description: If this string is an email address, i.e., a Mailbox, then the "xtext" syntax [32] SHOULD be used.

statements.subject: smtp
statements.description: Local-part = Dot-string / Quoted-string ; MAY be case-sensitive

statements.subject: server
statements.description: While the above definition for Local-part is relatively permissive, for maximum interoperability, a host that expects to receive mail SHOULD avoid defining mailboxes where the Local-part requires (or uses) the Quoted-string form or where the Local-part is case-sensitive.

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: For any purposes that require generating or comparing Local-parts (e.g., to specific mailbox names), all quoted forms MUST be treated as equivalent, and the sending system SHOULD transmit the form that uses the minimum quoting possible.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: For any purposes that require generating or comparing Local-parts (e.g., to specific mailbox names), all quoted forms MUST be treated as equivalent, and the sending system SHOULD transmit the form that uses the minimum quoting possible.

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: Systems MUST NOT define mailboxes in such a way as to require the use in SMTP of non-ASCII characters (octets with the high order bit set to one) or ASCII "control characters" (decimal value 0-31 and 127).

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: These characters MUST NOT be used in MAIL or RCPT commands or other commands that require mailbox names.

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: To promote interoperability and consistent with long-standing guidance about conservative use of the DNS in naming and applications (e.g., see Section 2.3.1 of the base DNS document, RFC 1035 [2]), characters outside the set of alphabetic characters, digits, and hyphen MUST NOT appear in domain name labels for SMTP clients or servers.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SMTP servers that receive a command in which invalid character codes have been employed, and for which there are no other reasons for rejection, MUST reject that command with a 501 response (this rule, like others, could be overridden by appropriate SMTP extensions).
